$comment: Every tunable number in combat/, party/ and the throw. GAME_DESIGN.md sections 5 and 7. No system file may restate any of these.

typeRing.$comment: Verdant beats Tide beats Ember beats Stone beats Spark beats Verdant. Each type beats exactly one and loses to exactly one, so no chart is needed to teach it.

stats.$comment: stat = floor(base * (1 + level * levelGain) * variance), variance rolled once at spawn and locked for life.

damage.$comment: dmg = (ATK/DEF) * movePower * typeMult * affinityMult * rand(rollMin,rollMax) * (1 + levelDiffPerLevel * levelDiff), floored at minimum so nothing is ever fully immune.

affinity.$comment: Above highThreshold a pal hits harder. Below lowThreshold it sometimes refuses a power attack. This is the emotional cost of the five-slot rule made mechanical.

charge.$comment: A power attack costs the full meter. Quick attacks build it by their own 'charge' value in moves.json.

pacing.$comment: How often the enemy acts. The delay scales inversely with SPD against referenceSpd, so a fast pal acts more often rather than hitting harder, which is what stops SPD being a stat nobody reads.

dodge.$comment: A dodge started inside the enemy telegraph negates the hit entirely. iframes are generous on purpose: this is a phone game and a swipe has latency a keypress does not.

flee.$comment: Wild pals bail at 20% HP with a 25% chance per second. This is the pressure that makes throwing early correct rather than grinding the enemy to 1 HP.

throw.$comment: Catch formula from GAME_DESIGN.md section 7, verbatim. The clamp is what guarantees no throw is ever certain and none is ever hopeless.

xp.$comment: xpToNext(level) = curveA * level^curveB. A win awards winBase * defeatedLevel, multiplied when the type ring favoured you. Benched party members take partyShare of it.

revive.$comment: A fainted pal is never lost. Four minutes of real time, or thirty seconds at a campfire.

encounter.$comment: Walking within triggerRange of a pal starts a fight. Aggressive species start it themselves from further out.

party.$comment: The number this whole game is built around. Enforced in Party.add() and nowhere else.
